interpretation.tier2: The §4.5 main-fixture tier2 trace is physically byte-identical before and after R35. It does reach the outer boundary in the release measurement window (tick 398 onward), but the collision path is unchanged.
interpretation.tier3: The tier3 trace already reaches the boundary before R35. After R35 it reaches the boundary sooner in the release window and has more wall-contact frames; it is not a clean no-wall measurement after the fix.
interpretation.mechanism: The first physical divergence is on a high-speed wall-grazing segment (tick 265). Reverse input is false there, and the static-steering fallback is inactive at that speed. The relevant R35 path change is the collision contact tolerance/reresolution branch, not a drift parameter.
interpretation.answer: The selective §4.7 change is a collision-environment change on the tier3 grazing path, not evidence that the drift parameter became stronger. The specific hypothesis “R35 no longer sticks to the wall” is false: both versions touch the wall, and R35 touches it earlier/more in the measured window. Therefore 5.873 is not a verified wall-free truth; 3.595 was also measured on a wall-interacting path.

before.contact_definition: wall_contact is direct snapshot wallContact when available, otherwise geometric_boundary_contact reconstructed from distance_to_nearest_boundary <= 1e-6 because a2cfc37 has no wallContact field

after.contact_definition: wall_contact is direct snapshot wallContact when available, otherwise geometric_boundary_contact reconstructed from distance_to_nearest_boundary <= 1e-6 because a2cfc37 has no wallContact field
